definition: Reincarnation is the return of existence in a new embodied life after death. In the source passage, it is described in connection with Hindu thought as a new life brought about by surviving karma rather than by a soul continuing unchanged through the interval after death.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Intermediate; pinned source text

reasons: The packet’s source text is about “Intermediate State,” not a definition of “reincarnation,” so the requested sense is not supported by the source packet.

The statement that reincarnation is “the return of existence in a new embodied life after death” is not given in the packet; the packet only says that in Hindu eschatology “only Karma survives to lead to a reincarnation.”
The claim that the source passage contrasts reincarnation with a soul “continuing unchanged through the interval after death” is not supported by the packet text.
The provided definition makes broad claims about reincarnation (“return of existence in a new embodied life after death”) but the packet excerpt does not define reincarnation in those terms.

The packet discusses an “Intermediate State” and says that in Hindu eschatology “the soul perishes at death, and only Karma survives to lead to a reincarnation,” but it does not describe reincarnation as a “new embodied life” nor provide a general characterization of reincarnation beyond that brief mention.

The definition’s comparison about “a soul continuing unchanged through the interval after death” is not explicitly stated in the packet (the packet instead states the opposite for Hindu eschatology: the soul does not properly exist in the interval).
Because the packet does not actually supply the requested term-sense of “reincarnation,” the definition relies on unsupported elaboration rather than only what is present in the source passage.
